factual_claims.claim: TKM Grupp AS reported a weaker financial performance in 2025 amid a challenging Estonian economic environment, low consumer confidence, intense retail competition and the introduction of Estonia’s motor vehicle tax.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The year 2025 will go down in history as a year of a challenging economic environment and major challenges for Estonian retailers in general and for TKM Group in particular. Consumer confidence remained low due to both the uncertain geopolitical situation and domestic tax changes. The introduction of the motor vehicle tax and contradictory government messaging throughout the year had a strong impact on the Estonian automotive retail sector. Competition in retail trade remained intense and consumer price sensitivity high.

Its revenue decreased 11.9% to €176.9 million, EBITDA fell 40.3% to €8.1 million and net profit declined 54.4% to €4.3 million.
Estonia’s new passenger-car market contracted 48.6%, with the motor vehicle tax and weakened consumer confidence cited as significant factors.
More stable sales in Latvia and Lithuania partly offset the decline.

verified_key_information_units.information: The supermarket segment increased revenue by 0.3% to 611.9 million euros but net profit fell 38.6% to 9.5 million euros, driven by economic weakness, promotional pricing pressure, and one-off costs from store refurbishments; strategic investments included logistics center optimization and assortment expansion with the First Price range.

candidate_sentences.text: The supermarkets segment generated modest revenue growth of 0.3% to €611.9 million, but net profit fell 38.6% to €9.5 million, reflecting lower sales volumes, increased promotional activity, wage-cost pressure and one-off costs associated with the Jõgeva Selver refurbishment.

verified_key_information_units.information: The department stores segment recorded a 1.1% revenue decline to 103.0 million euros and a net loss of 0.5 million euros, affected by warmer winter conditions; strategic actions included refurbishment of Kaubamaja Children’s World and launch of the Anni Arro café, with e-shop upgrades planned for 2026.

candidate_sentences.text: Department-store revenue declined 1.1% to €103.0 million and the segment recorded a €0.5 million net loss.

verified_key_information_units.information: The real estate segment increased revenue by 5.1% to 7.7 million euros but profit before tax fell 18.4% to 9.0 million euros, primarily due to one-off gains in 2024; rental income from the newly operational logistics centre offset declines from prior-year property sales.

candidate_sentences.text: Real-estate revenue increased 5.1% to €7.7 million, while net profit rose 20.5% to €6.3 million; the comparison was affected by €4.0 million of one-off gains in 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: Cash and cash equivalents decreased to 29.5 million euros (from 45.5 million euros in 2024), with working capital turning negative at 14.2 million euros; management confirms strong operating cash flow mitigates liquidity risk despite short-term loan maturities in 2026.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic expansion in the car segment includes the January 2026 agreement to acquire Rohe Auto AS and SKO Motors OÜ (Škoda distribution rights) in Estonia, enhancing brand portfolio and dealership network; 2025 also saw a new multi-brand showroom in Vilnius and ongoing bodywork workshop construction in Peetri.
